title: AIG-CIM: A Scalable Chiplet Module with Tri-Gear Heterogeneous Compute-in-Memory for Diffusion Acceleration
problem: Diffusion models face hardware deployment challenges due to unique computational requirements and flexible data reuse demands that exceed GPU efficiency for inference. Hardware accelerators must efficiently support the heterogeneous compute and memory access patterns characteristic of diffusion model inference.
motivation: Diffusion models are emerging as powerful AI-generated content generators but lack efficient specialized hardware acceleration, limiting practical deployment and real-time inference capabilities.
method: AIG-CIM uses compute-in-memory—placing calculations right alongside stored data to avoid slow data movement—with three different types of compute-in-memory units, each optimized for different parts of diffusion model inference. These units are distributed across scalable chiplets (separate mini-chips that can be connected together), allowing flexible data reuse because data stays near the computation. The entire system was built in TSMC 22nm technology, with careful optimization spanning from individual circuit design to how the multiple chiplets coordinate as a complete system.
key_novelty: Three different types of compute-in-memory units that scale across chiplets to enable flexible data-reuse patterns for diffusion model inference.
contributions: Tri-gear heterogeneous CIM architecture enabling flexible data reuse for diffusion workloads
Scalable chiplet-based design methodology for diffusion acceleration
21.3× latency reduction and 231.2× throughput improvement over RTX 3090
Three orders of magnitude energy efficiency improvement through CIM-based computation
limitations: Power/thermal management strategies and scalability limits not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: CIM-based scalable accelerator for efficient diffusion model inference
